content:
Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito warned Thursday that Congress has the power to effectively “turn off the lights” at the highest court by cutting off funding, less than two weeks after Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate.

“Congress can turn off the lights at the Supreme Court and stop everything from happening if they want to defund their activities. And there are many, many, many other things that they can do, or at least try to do,” Alito said at the Federalist Society’s annual Antonin Scalia Memorial Dinner, according to The Hill.

Alito, 76, notably did not mention the midterm elections, President Donald Trump’s attacks against federal judges who rule against him, or the incoming Democratic majorities in Congress during his speech to a crowd of more than 1,000 conservative lawyers.

But he did turn his criticism toward lower-court judges, chastising them for issuing what he called “unjustified” orders blocking presidents’ policies in recent years.

“They are dedicated and they are skillful, but they’re not perfect and they make mistakes,” he said. “And in some instances, I think they have gone far astray in abuse of their powers.”

Federal judges have repeatedly halted pieces of Trump’s agenda since he returned to office, drawing sharp attacks from the White House and its allies.

Alito’s remarks also come as Republicans grapple with what an incoming Democratic Senate means for the court. He and Justice Clarence Thomas, 78, have both said prior to the current term that they don’t plan to retire even if Democrats win the Senate, which has raised GOP worries that their seats won’t be filled under a Republican president and Senate.

The Federalist Society says it doesn’t take official positions, but it has long served as a pipeline for Republican judicial nominees, including several of the sitting justices.
